bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Project execution and management risk across a large, dispersed project portfolio — NBCC executes projects across project management consultancy, engineering procurement and construction, redevelopment and real estate, delivering complex infrastructure and real estate projects across multiple sectors and geographies, with each project carrying distinct commercial, contractual, regulatory and execution considerations. As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 317 running project locations (310 domestic and 7 international) plus 32 domestic and 4 international SBG/RBG offices. 'Project Execution and Management' is a named risk area mitigated through integrated planning, milestone reviews and stakeholder coordination, and the Company has strengthened internal controls, revised contractual frameworks and introduced greater operational flexibility to reduce disputes and manage execution-related risks.
- Aged receivables and payables — A named priority risk area mitigated through milestone billing, receivable monitoring and payment follow-up. It sits alongside project execution in the Company's own risk register, reflecting the cash-cycle exposure of a contractor-delivered project business.
- Redevelopment project risk — Redevelopment projects are a named risk area mitigated through due diligence, regulatory engagement and phased implementation. NBCC's redevelopment of GPRA colonies runs under self-sustainable models where risk is evaluated at every stage from project acquisition and planning through delivery and monetisation, so approval delays or slower monetisation feed straight into project outcomes.
- Real estate inventory and land risk — A named risk area addressed through portfolio optimization, targeted sales and land value maximization - unsold inventory and carried land tie up capital until monetised.
- Commodity price and market fluctuation risk — The Company is subject to commodity price risks due to fluctuation in prices of raw material used in the Company's projects, and 'Market Fluctuation' is a named risk area mitigated through dynamic costing, vendor diversification and procurement planning. The Company states it has a robust risk management framework for identification, monitoring and mitigation of risks of all kinds.
- Board and Board-committee composition non-compliance — The Company reports that as on March 31, 2026 it had complied with all mandatory requirements of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 except for the non-compliances relating to composition of the Board and certain Board Committees, as disclosed in the Report and in the Corporate Governance Compliance Certificate / Secretarial Audit Report - a governance exposure that persisted through FY 2025-26.
- Competition risk — A named risk area mitigated through selective bidding, differentiated offerings and client retention, reflecting that new work must be won competitively even for an established government implementation partner.
- Risk from entry into new business domains and external project takeover — Two named risk areas: entry into new business domains is mitigated through capability building, strategic partnerships and phased entry, while external project takeover is mitigated through due diligence, escrow mechanisms and structured project planning. Both take the Company beyond its established execution profile, and geopolitical risk is one of the dimensions the risk framework explicitly covers alongside technical, commercial, operational and regulatory risk.

outlook.body:
- Operate on a debt-free, asset-light and execution-driven management philosophy that leverages Navratna CPSE status, functioning simultaneously as Project Management Consultant, EPC contractor and real estate developer with a mandate to deliver critical government infrastructure.
- The self-sustainable redevelopment model is the cornerstone: NBCC develops dilapidated government colonies and office complexes on prime land and monetises a portion of the commercial and residential space to recover the entire construction cost, so large-scale redevelopment is delivered without financial burden on the exchequer and without external borrowings.
- Sustain debt-free growth by continuing to fund expansion through internal resources and client funding rather than bank borrowings, with client advances received from ministries and departments at project outset.
- Reinvest in the core businesses - PMC services, EPC execution and redevelopment projects - to strengthen capabilities and scale.
- Execute strategic government redevelopment projects that transform urban infrastructure while being self-financing.
- Strengthen reserves and enhance shareholder returns through consistent performance and prudent financial management, preserving financial strength and operational independence.
- Expand the use of digital technologies across the project lifecycle, integrating tendering, design, execution and asset handover, while building on established capabilities in PMC, EPC, redevelopment and real estate.
- Broaden the portfolio through complex domestic and international assignments as a trusted implementation partner to Government ministries, departments and public institutions.
- Keep the order book diversified across government ministries, public sector enterprises and statutory authorities to reduce dependence on individual projects or client categories.
- Deploy surplus funds through disciplined treasury management to generate interest income that supplements the prudent margin profile inherent to the PMC business.
- Maintain a Quality Management System under ISO 9001:2015 covering all activities carried out for providing Project Management Consultancy and execution of projects, with internal ISO audits of identified project sites every six months and of service departments annually.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: NBCC describes itself as having an asset-light and debt-free structure with a lean operating model, and its growth comes from a larger project portfolio rather than from owned manufacturing capacity, so this bundle describes capability build-out rather than plant capex. During FY 2025-26 the Company focused on 'Building Execution Capacity': it increased the use of prefabrication, precast components and modular construction to reduce site-intensive activity, reporting a 20-30% reduction in construction timelines on select projects using modular and prefabricated methods, with factory-controlled production reducing variability and defects, and tower cranes, mechanised scaffolding and ready-mix concrete plants reducing dependence on manual processes; Method Statements and SOPs standardised workflows to limit rework. Digital build-out included Building Information Modelling (BIM) and shared data platforms on selected projects, giving architects, engineers and contractors a single coordinated 3D model for clash detection and real-time access to drawings, schedules and material data, with integration to IPMS linking design data to procurement and construction schedules. Institutional-knowledge capacity was extended through a Project Archive Module in the ERP storing lessons learnt and as-built drawings, after-action reviews and best-practice circulars, and reuse of past learning in DPRs, tender templates and employee training. Site-safety infrastructure was scaled with smart monitoring of air quality, dust, noise and temperature, CCTV surveillance of large sites, engineering controls (ELCBs, backfire arrestors, reverse vehicle alarms) and third-party inspections, with 120 project sites safety-audited against a target of 100. Human capacity stood at 1,150 employees as on 31 March 2026, supported by 137 training and capacity-building programmes and 3,766 training man-days, plus a Succession Planning and Leadership Development Plan implemented in concurrence with the Capacity Building Commission, Government of India. On the corporate-structure side, a Scheme of Arrangement for the merger of wholly-owned subsidiary HSCC (India) Limited with NBCC has been proposed under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, and NBCC Overseas Real Estate LLC became a subsidiary during FY 2025-26. The rupee capital commitments the Company does disclose are modest and relate to office renovation, retro-fitting, MEP services and interior works rather than to productive capacity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Infrastructure development remained a key priority for the Government of India, providing impetus to construction, real estate and project management activity, and expanding the project pipeline for organisations engaged in infrastructure development, redevelopment and PMC services.
- Government capital expenditure reached Rs 11.0 lakh crore in FY 2025-26 and is proposed to rise to Rs 12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27, with continued focus on infrastructure expansion and timely execution of projects.
- The Union Budget 2026-27 positions infrastructure as one of the seven strategic and frontier pillars supporting India's long-term economic growth.
- India recorded a GDP growth rate of 7.7% in FY 2026, with gross fixed capital formation growing around 8.2% and credit from all sources increasing 13.8% year-on-year, supporting construction demand.
- Real estate and ownership of dwellings has contributed around 7% of annual GVA on average over the past decade; housing demand benefited from favourable affordability conditions and easing inflation, with average sales volumes staying above FY 2022-24 levels.
- Housing demand is projected to reach around 93 Mn units by 2036, and India's office real estate market is expected to require an additional 1.7 Bn sq ft of office space over the next decade, offering a potential revenue opportunity of approximately $125 Bn by 2034.
- Growth in office spaces, logistics and industrial facilities is increasing construction demand, supported by expansion of technology corridors, rising multinational investments and integrated industrial townships.
- Large-scale infrastructure projects including highways, logistics corridors and water infrastructure continue to drive demand for engineering and construction services.
- The global construction market was valued at approximately $16.45 trillion in CY 2025, up from $15.78 trillion in CY 2024, with emerging economies in Asia-Pacific accounting for a significant share.
- Policy programmes underpinning demand include PMAY-U 2.0 (an additional 2.88 lakh houses approved, taking total sanctions to 13.61 lakh units, plus 12,800 rental housing projects), the Smart Cities Mission (100 cities, 8,067 projects, Rs 1.64 lakh crore investment, around 94% completed), PMGSY-IV (Rs 70,125 crore outlay for approximately 62,500 km of all-weather roads), Housing for All - Urban, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, RERA and RCS-UDAN.
- The construction industry is increasingly defined by three pillars - digital transparency, multimodal efficiency and mandatory sustainability - and is moving from a phase of recovery to one of rapid execution.
- Real estate markets operated against a gradually improving financing environment as inflation moderated, with investment activity selective and demand concentrated across housing, logistics, data centres and urban redevelopment.
- Headwinds flagged: prolonged geopolitical tensions, global trade volatility and climate-related risks may moderate the pace of growth; the Strait of Hormuz crisis pressured oil and gas prices and India's energy security, US tariffs disrupted international trade, the Russia-Ukraine war continued to affect supply chains, and a developing El Nino event could persist well into 2027.
- Margin context: the Company operates with a prudent margin profile inherent to the PMC business but continues to generate healthy returns on equity, with disciplined treasury management and structured deployment of surplus funds contributing meaningful interest income.
- The consolidated work order book at the end of the year stood at Rs 1,27,820 crore, across redevelopment, Project Management Consultancy, engineering procurement and construction, infrastructure and international assignments.
- New Consolidated Business Secured during the year totalled Rs 18,780 crore and the works Awarded stood at Rs 11,546 crore.
- The order book is diversified across government ministries, public sector enterprises and statutory authorities, alongside redevelopment, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, commercial developments and international assignments - broadening the execution pipeline and reducing dependence on individual projects or client categories.
- Projects progress across different stages of execution and approval cycles; activity across redevelopment, institutional infrastructure, healthcare, education, residential developments and overseas assignments provides a balanced mix of opportunities throughout the project lifecycle.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Infrastructure development remained a key priority for the Government of India, providing impetus to construction, real estate and project management activity, and expanding the project pipeline for organisations engaged in infrastructure development, redevelopment and PMC services.
- Government capital expenditure reached Rs 11.0 lakh crore in FY 2025-26 and is proposed to rise to Rs 12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27, with continued focus on infrastructure expansion and timely execution of projects.
- The Union Budget 2026-27 positions infrastructure as one of the seven strategic and frontier pillars supporting India's long-term economic growth.
- India recorded a GDP growth rate of 7.7% in FY 2026, with gross fixed capital formation growing around 8.2% and credit from all sources increasing 13.8% year-on-year, supporting construction demand.
- Real estate and ownership of dwellings has contributed around 7% of annual GVA on average over the past decade; housing demand benefited from favourable affordability conditions and easing inflation, with average sales volumes staying above FY 2022-24 levels.
- Housing demand is projected to reach around 93 Mn units by 2036, and India's office real estate market is expected to require an additional 1.7 Bn sq ft of office space over the next decade, offering a potential revenue opportunity of approximately $125 Bn by 2034.
- Growth in office spaces, logistics and industrial facilities is increasing construction demand, supported by expansion of technology corridors, rising multinational investments and integrated industrial townships.
- Large-scale infrastructure projects including highways, logistics corridors and water infrastructure continue to drive demand for engineering and construction services.
- The global construction market was valued at approximately $16.45 trillion in CY 2025, up from $15.78 trillion in CY 2024, with emerging economies in Asia-Pacific accounting for a significant share.
- Policy programmes underpinning demand include PMAY-U 2.0 (an additional 2.88 lakh houses approved, taking total sanctions to 13.61 lakh units, plus 12,800 rental housing projects), the Smart Cities Mission (100 cities, 8,067 projects, Rs 1.64 lakh crore investment, around 94% completed), PMGSY-IV (Rs 70,125 crore outlay for approximately 62,500 km of all-weather roads), Housing for All - Urban, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, RERA and RCS-UDAN.
- The construction industry is increasingly defined by three pillars - digital transparency, multimodal efficiency and mandatory sustainability - and is moving from a phase of recovery to one of rapid execution.
- Real estate markets operated against a gradually improving financing environment as inflation moderated, with investment activity selective and demand concentrated across housing, logistics, data centres and urban redevelopment.
- Headwinds flagged: prolonged geopolitical tensions, global trade volatility and climate-related risks may moderate the pace of growth; the Strait of Hormuz crisis pressured oil and gas prices and India's energy security, US tariffs disrupted international trade, the Russia-Ukraine war continued to affect supply chains, and a developing El Nino event could persist well into 2027.
- Margin context: the Company operates with a prudent margin profile inherent to the PMC business but continues to generate healthy returns on equity, with disciplined treasury management and structured deployment of surplus funds contributing meaningful interest income.
- The consolidated work order book at the end of the year stood at Rs 1,27,820 crore, across redevelopment, Project Management Consultancy, engineering procurement and construction, infrastructure and international assignments.
- New Consolidated Business Secured during the year totalled Rs 18,780 crore and the works Awarded stood at Rs 11,546 crore.
- The order book is diversified across government ministries, public sector enterprises and statutory authorities, alongside redevelopment, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, commercial developments and international assignments - broadening the execution pipeline and reducing dependence on individual projects or client categories.
- Projects progress across different stages of execution and approval cycles; activity across redevelopment, institutional infrastructure, healthcare, education, residential developments and overseas assignments provides a balanced mix of opportunities throughout the project lifecycle.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: NBCC describes itself as having an asset-light and debt-free structure with a lean operating model, and its growth comes from a larger project portfolio rather than from owned manufacturing capacity, so this bundle describes capability build-out rather than plant capex. During FY 2025-26 the Company focused on 'Building Execution Capacity': it increased the use of prefabrication, precast components and modular construction to reduce site-intensive activity, reporting a 20-30% reduction in construction timelines on select projects using modular and prefabricated methods, with factory-controlled production reducing variability and defects, and tower cranes, mechanised scaffolding and ready-mix concrete plants reducing dependence on manual processes; Method Statements and SOPs standardised workflows to limit rework. Digital build-out included Building Information Modelling (BIM) and shared data platforms on selected projects, giving architects, engineers and contractors a single coordinated 3D model for clash detection and real-time access to drawings, schedules and material data, with integration to IPMS linking design data to procurement and construction schedules. Institutional-knowledge capacity was extended through a Project Archive Module in the ERP storing lessons learnt and as-built drawings, after-action reviews and best-practice circulars, and reuse of past learning in DPRs, tender templates and employee training. Site-safety infrastructure was scaled with smart monitoring of air quality, dust, noise and temperature, CCTV surveillance of large sites, engineering controls (ELCBs, backfire arrestors, reverse vehicle alarms) and third-party inspections, with 120 project sites safety-audited against a target of 100. Human capacity stood at 1,150 employees as on 31 March 2026, supported by 137 training and capacity-building programmes and 3,766 training man-days, plus a Succession Planning and Leadership Development Plan implemented in concurrence with the Capacity Building Commission, Government of India. On the corporate-structure side, a Scheme of Arrangement for the merger of wholly-owned subsidiary HSCC (India) Limited with NBCC has been proposed under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, and NBCC Overseas Real Estate LLC became a subsidiary during FY 2025-26. The rupee capital commitments the Company does disclose are modest and relate to office renovation, retro-fitting, MEP services and interior works rather than to productive capacity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths

- 65+ years of experience since establishment in 1960, with an 'Excellent' rating in the 2024-25 MoU evaluation scoring 97.58 - a second consecutive year in the highest category and top performer in the Consultancy & Construction sector
- Navratna CPSE status under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, making it a preferred implementation partner for Ministries, Government Departments and Public Sector Institutions
- Asset-light and debt-free structure - physical execution is entrusted to contractors, supporting financial flexibility and scalable growth
- Self-sustainable redevelopment framework where projects are undertaken jointly by government authorities and NBCC, combining commercial monetisation with urban transformation
- Integrated capability across PMC, EPC and Real Estate within one organisation
- Consolidated order book of Rs 1,27,820 crore as on March 31, 2026 providing sustained revenue visibility
- Execution strengthened by subsidiaries HSCC (India) Ltd., Hindustan Steelworks Construction Limited (HSCL) and NBCC Services Limited (NSL), enabling specialised healthcare infrastructure, steel plant construction and facility management projects
- 99% of procurement routed through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), supporting transparency in public procurement
- Digital execution stack - Building Information Modelling, ERP, Office 365, a Vendor Portal and AI-driven design optimisation, predictive project monitoring, risk assessment and quality assurance
